reconcile.connective: Defenders read Nachon and Chidon as two names for one place — Gill takes them as alternate names for the same threshing-floor.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who notes the two accounts of the same incident name the location differently — Nachon's threshing-floor in 2 Samuel but Chidon's in 1 Chronicles.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("Where did God kill Uzzah?", skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/uzza.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Who is called Chidon, Ch1 13:9; he seems to have had two names; or it was a place that had two names, as say the Jews …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly harmonizes the exact place-name difference (Nachon vs Chidon) by treating them as two names for one place — the precise tension of this row.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on 2 Samuel 6:6-7
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat the Nachon/Chidon difference at the verse, reading Chidon as an explanation of Nachon — the threshing-floor named from the incident, not its owner; harmonizing commentator surfaced on the row (Haley's coverage of this specific pair unconfirmed).
